Chapter One

The Problem

In the crucial moments of choice, we try to self-regulate by scrolling, eating, shopping — or worse.

Global anxiety, loneliness, emotional dysregulation, and polarization are at historic highs.

While mindfulness and meditation have entered mainstream culture, many people still lack practical tools to regulate fear, stress, and reactivity in real-world situations. Existing information often intellectualizes emotional and mental health. It lacks measurable tools and outcomes, and it fails to reach non-spiritual audiences.

So in the crucial moments of choice, we try to self-regulate by scrolling. Eating. Shopping. Or worse.

Empathy: The Pursuit of Joy is a premium, 90-minute feature documentary and a streaming series: a cinematic sonic experience, combining ancient wisdom, proven by science, to use in our lives — with measured mind, body, and soul impact.

“Ancient wisdom, proven by science, to use in our lives.
✦
Chapter Two

Our Unprecedented Approach

Our goal? Scientifically prove that empathy, compassion, and joy affect personal well-being.

We bring together ancient traditions, practices, and wisdom — the foundation of personal transformation — with neuroscience and real-world stories from ordinary people who have applied the teachings to navigate real-world challenges.

Our goal is to scientifically prove that empathy, compassion, and joy affect personal well-being. And to deliver empathy as an embodied, experiential intervention — using story, music, and neuroscience so audiences feel, understand, and apply empathy and compassion in their daily life.

With music as the universal self-regulation language, we bridge science and emotional intelligence, making the ancient wisdom accessible — and fun.

✦
Chapter Three

Music Is the Universal Language

The film's sound-bath soundtrack is designed to help you access your own joy.

Music is the universal self-regulation language. It reaches the body before the mind has finished arguing, which is exactly why we built the film around it.

The film's sound-bath soundtrack is designed to help you access your own joy. Our renowned scientific team is scientifically proving that art and music are more than cultural artifacts — in an original sound-bath soundtrack and score.

And we add the most important element.

“Art and music are more than cultural artifacts.
✦
Chapter Four

The Dalai Lama Is a Scientist

Thirty-plus years of scientifically documenting what compassion does to a human being.

Our film highlights the Dalai Lama's leadership in coordinating and collaborating with prominent neuroscientists and researchers from Harvard, UC San Diego, Stanford, Wisconsin, Columbia, and Emory University — who have spent thirty-plus years scientifically documenting the biomarker and positive-mindset changes from compassion, empathy, and consciousness.

Emory University is our education partner. Dr. Lobsang, head of the Emory Compassion Center, brings Emory's books, courses, and consulting to the film and to everyone it reaches.

✦
Chapter Five

The Monks, the Nuns and the Scientists

They come together to show us new ways of being.

The monks, the nuns, and the scientists come together to show us new ways of being. Mingyur Rinpoche and Dr. Richard Davidson of the University of Wisconsin. The contemplatives who have practised for decades, and the researchers who finally had instruments precise enough to see what the practice does.

This is not a film about belief. It is a film about what happens in a human body, filmed from both sides of the instrument.

“New ways of being — filmed from both sides of the instrument.
✦
Chapter Six

The Scientists Bring the Proof

Over 17 million people. 24 countries. 22 languages. Studied at Emory University alone.

Over seventeen million people, across twenty-four countries and twenty-two languages, have been studied at Emory University alone.

These neuroscientists measured how empathy and compassion rewire your brain and increase your resilience. Not metaphorically. Measurably — in biomarkers, in psychological outcomes, in what a person can carry after the practice that they could not carry before.

That is the proof the film brings. And it is the proof you can have first-hand.

✦
Chapter Seven

The Film Becomes an Immersive Museum

Think the Van Gogh exhibit. Think Dataland.

Projection-scale storytelling. Five-senses-responsive art. Acoustic spatial architecture. Music-guided sound baths, and moments of reflection.

All of it designed around self-regulation and co-regulation — and feeling awesome. The film becomes an immersive museum experience, so more people can experience the translated wisdom with their whole body, not just their eyes.

“Designed around self-regulation and co-regulation — and feeling awesome.

Chapter Eight

It's Not About Becoming a Monk

This film reveals the science and the secrets to unlock your inner wisdom and joy.

So whether you are a parent, a founder, a teacher, a nurse, a police officer, or a person who has simply had enough of the scrolling — this film reveals the science and the secrets to unlock your inner wisdom and joy.

It's not about becoming a monk. It's not about changing your religion. It's not about meditating on mountaintops.

It is about what the monks and the scientists both found, and how to use it on a Tuesday.

“To joy.
